research_gaps: Robust cross‑domain generalization: current self‑supervised models still degrade sharply when tested on scenes with different lighting, camera intrinsics, or scene semantics (e.g., sports broadcast vs. driving).
Dynamic and non‑rigid motion modelling: pose networks assume a static scene; moving objects and deformable bodies cause depth leaks and artefacts.
Unified lightweight architecture that jointly predicts depth, surface normals, and semantic cues while remaining real‑time on edge hardware.

proposals.name: Domain‑Adaptive Multi‑Task Transformer (DA‑MTT)
proposals.rationale: Combine a shared Vision Transformer encoder with three task heads (depth, surface normal, semantic segmentation). Train with self‑supervised photometric loss on source domains (KITTI, NYU) and a domain‑adversarial loss that aligns feature distributions to target domains (e.g., SoccerNet).
proposals.expected_benefit: Improves generalization across drastically different visual domains by leveraging shared geometric semantics; the multi‑task signals regularize depth predictions on unseen data.
proposals.risk: Adversarial alignment can be unstable; adding multiple heads increases memory, challenging strict real‑time constraints.

proposals.name: Dynamic‑Mask Pose‑Refinement (DM‑PR) Module
proposals.rationale: Introduce a lightweight motion‑segmentation branch that predicts per‑pixel dynamic masks; use these masks to weight the photometric reprojection loss and to fine‑tune the pose network via a residual refinement block trained end‑to‑end.
proposals.expected_benefit: Reduces depth errors caused by moving objects and non‑rigid bodies, directly addressing the dominant failure mode highlighted by SPIdepth and SoccerNet benchmarks.
proposals.risk: Accurate dynamic masking may require additional supervision or careful curriculum learning; errors in mask prediction can propagate to pose refinement, hurting overall performance.

proposals.name: Efficient Diffusion‑Based Depth Prior (EDDP)
proposals.rationale: Leverage a pre‑trained diffusion model to generate a coarse depth prior from a single image, then fuse it with the self‑supervised depth estimate using a fast bilateral refinement network.
proposals.expected_benefit: Provides a global, scene‑consistent depth scaffold that helps recover structure in texture‑less or reflective regions where photometric loss fails, without adding inference cost beyond a single forward pass of a lightweight diffusion encoder.
proposals.risk: Diffusion models are typically large; distilling them into an efficient encoder may lose fidelity, and the prior could bias the network toward training‑set statistics, limiting adaptability.
